subject: EU / APAC residency: edge split policy + fallback proposal
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@northbank.eu>, Sato Yamaguchi <sato.yamaguchi@tokyo-fin.co.jp>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU / APAC residency: edge split policy + fallback proposal

Hi Liam / Sato —

Following our workshop last week, attached is a short draft (residency-edge-split-draft-v1.pdf) that outlines a proposed "edge split" for NorthBank: EU primary (Frankfurt/Amsterdam PoPs) with APAC (Tokyo/Singapore) as warm standby for select workloads. High-level asks we had from your side: no persistent egress from EU to APAC for regulated PII, audit logs must be retained in-region, and any KMS usage must be EU-hosted keys.

Key questions for you before we lock the design:
- Which datasets are DR-eligible to cross region (if any)?
- Do you require a customer-managed KMS (HSM) in the EU for all keys or only for production token signing?
- Are there procurement constraints around cross-border BGP/peering (we can offer transit via our partner in EU to avoid direct peering if preferred)?

Technical notes included in the attachment: routing policy (in-region ingress endpoints + route-anchoring using Transit GW), DNS-based weighted routing with short TTLs for failover, and an audit/telemetry endpoint that keeps logs in Frankfurt S3 bucket with read-only replication to a NorthBank-controlled archive (if allowed).

Can you confirm if the KMS constraint is absolute? If yes, we'll propose a design that never egresses encrypted payloads out of EU and keeps KV caches pinned to EU hosts.

Next steps: if you can confirm the three questions above by EOD Tue (20 Apr), we'll produce an operational checklist and runbook sections for your security review.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+44 20 7 555 0142

Attachments: residency-edge-split-draft-v1.pdf, SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@northbank.eu>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sato Yamaguchi <sato.yamaguchi@tokyo-fin.co.jp>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement <procure@northbank.eu>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 13:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU / APAC residency: edge split policy + fallback proposal

Rachel —

Thanks for the draft. Quick clarifications from our side:
- No EU-origin PII may be processed outside the EU. That means any unencrypted payload or decrypted KV must remain in EU. Encrypted backups may replicate to APAC only if keys are EU-resident and NorthBank retains control.
- Procurement: we prefer not to do new direct peering with unknown transit providers. If Redwood can present a certification or operate via an approved partner, that will help.
- KMS: Production keys must be customer-managed and located in our Frankfurt tenant (we can provide HSM access).

Please include an explicit egress-policy section in the runbook that lists allowed and disallowed flows. Also include acceptance test steps we can run (sample payloads, telemetry checks).

I'll loop in procurement formally next week to discuss contract language for data movement and HSM access.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Architecture | NorthBank
liam.oconnor@northbank.eu

Attachment: northbank-residency-reqs.docx (referenced)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: EU / APAC residency: edge split policy + fallback proposal

On Fri, 17 Apr 2027 at 09:12, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following our workshop last week, attached is a short draft...

Thanks Rachel — I sketched out a technical follow-up to cover the egress and failover mechanics Liam requested. High-level bullets:
- In-region processing: all decryption/KV caches pinned to EU hosts via node affinity and strict route tables. No KV cache replication to APAC for EU-scoped customers.
- KMS: support customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM). We will integrate with their Frankfurt KMS endpoint via a dedicated peering tunnel and use short-lived session tokens issued by NorthBank's HSM.
- Network: prefer using your approved transit partner in EU to avoid new direct AS peering. We'll present BGP poster child config and MTU checks.
- Failover: DNS-weighted shift (TTL 30s) + route-table failover for transit + optional automatic model fallback (EU -> smaller EU-only fallback model) before any cross-border traffic is attempted. Cross-border failover only allowed for non-PII workloads and only after manual authorization.
- Telemetry: audit logs will be written to Frankfurt S3, encrypted with the customer KMS; optional event-forwarding (read-only) to their archive. We'll provide a signed SHA-256 manifest for every replication batch for provable chain-of-custody.

I'm attaching a short checklist (I'll push to the Drive runbook link in related_links) that maps acceptance tests to runbook steps (BGP up/down, DNS failover, KMS key rotation test, log integrity verification).

Questions for Mina: any SOC2 or legal redlines we should pre-empt in the runbook language?

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Architect

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@northbank.eu>, Sato Yamaguchi <sato.yamaguchi@tokyo-fin.co.jp>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: EU / APAC residency: edge split policy + fallback proposal

Liam / Sato —

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary of agreed actions and owners: 
1) Redwood to update runbook with explicit egress-policy and acceptance tests (owner: rachel_kim) — target: 2027-04-22 EOD.
2) Karthik to produce a BGP / transit config appendix and HSM integration notes (owner: karthik_iyer) — target: 2027-04-21.
3) NorthBank to share formal KMS endpoint details and HSM access process (owner: Liam) — target: 2027-04-20.
4) Procurement to schedule contract language call (owner: procurement@northbank.eu) — target: the week of 2027-04-26.

We will mark the cross-border failover checkbox as MANUAL-ONLY for any EU-scoped PII workloads; automatic failover will be limited to non-PII with a pre-approved runbook. I will also attach the acceptance checklist to the DocuSign envelope once procurement confirms the semantics.

If that aligns, I'll publish the runbook update and send a short readout to your security team.

Best,
Rachel
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
